title: The Risk of Horizontal Sanitary Tees
description: Using a standard sanitary tee to connect a horizontal waste pipe into another horizontal line is a frequent error in drainage piping. Sanitary tees are engineered primarily for transitioning from horizontal runs into vertical stacks. When installed horizontally, the short sweep does not properly direct waste flow, causing solids to accumulate, flow backward, or create chronic blockages over time. Standard plumbing practices require wyes, combination wye and eighth bends, or long-turn fittings for horizontal-to-horizontal drainage connections to maintain proper directional flow and prevent solids from settling inside the fitting.

The Risk of Horizontal Sanitary Tees

Using a standard sanitary tee to connect a horizontal waste pipe into another horizontal line is a frequent error in drainage piping. Sanitary tees are engineered primarily for transitioning from horizontal runs into vertical stacks. When installed horizontally, the short sweep does not properly direct waste flow, causing solids to accumulate, flow backward, or create chronic blockages over time. Standard plumbing practices require wyes, combination wye and eighth bends, or long-turn fittings for horizontal-to-horizontal drainage connections to maintain proper directional flow and prevent solids from settling inside the fitting.
